   line 36:  p300.aspirate(bsa_vol, tubes["A1"])
   At line 36 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 0.39 ul, 0.78 ul, 1.56 ul, 3.12 ul and 2
   more, below its minimum of 20 ul (this line did it 6 times). A pipette cannot measure
   less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this
   protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [c498805d5d70]

2. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: water (well A1 in slot 3)
   line 40:  p300.aspirate(water_vol, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 40 the tip went into water (well A1 in slot 3) while it still carried bsa (tube
   A1 in slot 2) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of
   it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong
   there. The protocol drew from it again afterwards, but only into wells that were given
   that material on purpose anyway, so this run is not harmed. What is left in the stock is
   no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 40 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.

tool_calls.arguments:
{"text": "from opentrons import protocol_api

metadata = {"protocolName": "BSA Standard Curve", "apiLevel": "2.19"}

def run(protocol: protocol_api.ProtocolContext):
    # Load labware
    tips_300 = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_300ul", 1)
    tips_20 = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_20ul", 5)
    tubes = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_24_tuberack_nest_1.5ml_snapcap", 2)
    reservoir = protocol.load_labware("nest_12_reservoir_15ml", 3)
    plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat", 4)
    
    # Load pipettes
    p300 = protocol.load_instrument("p300_single_gen2", "right", tip_racks=[tips_300])
    p20 = protocol.load_instrument("p20_single_gen2", "left", tip_racks=[tips_20])
    
    # Define liquids
    bsa = protocol.define_liquid(name="bsa", description="BSA stock", display_color="#FF0000")
    water = protocol.define_liquid(name="water", description="Water", display_color="#0000FF")
    
    # Load liquids into source wells
    tubes["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=bsa, volume=1000)
    reservoir["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=water, volume=2000)
    
    # Destination wells and volumes
    dest_wells = ["A1", "A2", "A3", "A4", "A5", "A6", "A7", "A8"]
    bsa_volumes = [50, 25, 12.5, 6.25, 3.12, 1.56, 0.78, 0.39]
    water_volumes = [0, 25, 37.5, 43.75, 46.88, 48.44, 49.22, 49.61]
    
    # Prepare transfers
    for i in range(len(dest_wells)):
        dest = plate[dest_wells[i]]
        bsa_vol = bsa_volumes[i]
        water_vol = water_volumes[i]
        
        # Choose pipette for BSA transfer based on volume
        if bsa_vol > 20:
            aspirator = p300
        else:
            aspirator = p20
        
        # Aspirate and dispense BSA
        aspirator.pick_up_tip()
        aspirator.aspirate(bsa_vol, tubes["A1"])
        aspirator.dispense(bsa_vol, dest)
        aspirator.drop_tip()
        
        # Aspirate and dispense water if needed
        if water_vol > 0:
            p300.pick_up_tip()
            p300.aspirate(water_vol, reservoir["A1"])
            p300.dispense(water_vol, dest)
            p300.drop_tip()"}

tool_calls.name: write_protocol
tool_calls.arguments:
{"text": "from opentrons import protocol_api

metadata = {"protocolName": "BSA Standard Curve", "apiLevel": "2.19"}

def run(protocol: protocol_api.ProtocolContext):
    # Load labware
    tips_300 = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_300ul", 1)
    tubes = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_24_tuberack_nest_1.5ml_snapcap", 2)
    reservoir = protocol.load_labware("nest_12_reservoir_15ml", 3)
    plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat", 4)
    
    # Load pipette
    p300 = protocol.load_instrument("p300_single_gen2", "right", tip_racks=[tips_300])
    
    # Define liquids
    bsa = protocol.define_liquid(name="bsa", description="BSA stock", display_color="#FF0000")
    water = protocol.define_liquid(name="water", description="Water", display_color="#0000FF")
    
    # Load liquids into source wells
    tubes["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=bsa, volume=1000)
    reservoir["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=water, volume=2000)
    
    # Destination wells
    dest_wells = ["A1", "A2", "A2", "A3", "A4", "A5", "A6", "A7"]  # Using A2-A8 for standards, A1 for blank water
    
    # Dilution series parameters from plate map
    diluent_volumes = [0.0, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0]
    transfer_volumes = [100.0, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0]
    sources = ["stock", "well 1", "well 2", "well 3", "well 4", "well 5", "well 6", "well 7"]
    
    # Process each well
    for i in range(len(dest_wells)):
        dest = plate[dest_wells[i]]
        
        # Add diluent (water) if needed
        if diluent_volumes[i] > 0:
            p300.pick_up_tip()
            p300.aspirate(diluent_volumes[i], reservoir["A1"])
            p300.dispense(diluent_volumes[i], dest)
            p300.drop_tip()
        
        # Determine source well
        if sources[i] == "stock":
            source_well = tubes["A1"]
        else:
            source_num = int(sources[i].split()[1])
            source_well = plate["A" + str(source_num)]
        
        # Transfer stock (or mixture) into destination well
        p300.pick_up_tip()
        p300.aspirate(transfer_volumes[i], source_well)
        p300.dispense(transfer_volumes[i], dest)
        p300.drop_tip()
        
        # Mix: use 80% of well volume (80 ul) for 5 cycles
        mix_volume = 80.0
        for _ in range(5):
            p300.pick_up_tip()
            p300.aspirate(mix_volume, dest)
            p300.dispense(mix_volume, dest)
            p300.drop_tip()
        
        # Remove excess from last well (well 8)
        if i == 7:
            p300.pick_up_tip()
            p300.aspirate(50.0, dest)
            p300.drop_tip()"}

tool_calls.arguments:
{"text": "from opentrons import protocol_api

metadata = {"protocolName": "BSA Standard Curve", "apiLevel": "2.19"}

def run(protocol: protocol_api.ProtocolContext):
    # Load labware
    tips_300 = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_300ul", 1)
    tubes = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_24_tuberack_nest_1.5ml_snapcap", 2)
    reservoir = protocol.load_labware("nest_12_reservoir_15ml", 3)
    plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat", 4)
    
    # Load pipette
    p300 = protocol.load_instrument("p300_single_gen2", "right", tip_racks=[tips_300])
    
    # Define liquids
    bsa = protocol.define_liquid(name="bsa", description="BSA stock", display_color="#FF0000")
    water = protocol.define_liquid(name="water", description="Water", display_color="#0000FF")
    
    # Load liquids into source wells
    tubes["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=bsa, volume=1000)
    reservoir["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=water, volume=2000)
    
    # Destination wells for standards (A1-A8)
    dest_wells = ["A1", "A2", "A3", "A4", "A5", "A6", "A7", "A8"]
    
    # Volumes from plate map ( BSA then water for each well )
    bsa_volumes = [50, 25, 12.5, 6.25, 3.12, 1.56, 0.78, 0.39]
    water_volumes = [0, 25, 37.5, 43.75, 46.88, 48.44, 49.22, 49.61]
    
    # Process each well
    for i in range(len(dest_wells)):
        dest = plate[dest_wells[i]]
        bsa_vol = bsa_volumes[i]
        water_vol = water_volumes[i]
        
        # Add water diluent first
        if water_vol > 0:
            p300.pick_up_tip()
            p300.aspirate(water_vol, reservoir["A1"])
            p300.dispense(water_vol, dest)
            p300.drop_tip()
        
        # Transfer BSA
        p300.pick_up_tip()
        p300.aspirate(bsa_vol, tubes["A1"])
        p300.dispense(bsa_vol, dest)
        p300.drop_tip()
        
        # Mix: 80% of well volume (~80 ul) for 5 cycles
        mix_volume = 80.0
        for _ in range(5):
            p300.pick_up_tip()
            p300.aspirate(mix_volume, dest)
            p300.dispense(mix_volume, dest)
            p300.drop_tip()
        
        # Remove excess from last well (50 ul removal)
        if i == 7:  # Last well (A8)
            p300.pick_up_tip()
            p300.aspirate(50.0, dest)
            p300.drop_tip()"}

protocol.py: 3 biology problems (1 error, 1 warning, 1 note).

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 0.39 ul, 0.78 ul, 1.56 ul, 3.12 ul and 2 more are below what the
p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at least)
   line 45:  p300.aspirate(bsa_vol, tubes["A1"])
   At line 45 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 0.39 ul, 0.78 ul, 1.56 ul, 3.12 ul and 2
   more, below its minimum of 20 ul (this line did it 6 times). A pipette cannot measure
   less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this
   protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [c498805d5d70]

2. WARNING MIX-TOO-WEAK: Mixing too weak to stir 7 wells: 1 × 80 ul in 50 ul
   line 53:  p300.aspirate(mix_volume, dest)
   At line 53 the tip mixes wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 4 with 1 stroke of
   80 ul in a well holding 50 ul (this line did it 35 times). 1 stroke of 80 ul move 1.6 of
   the well in all; it takes about 2 wells' worth of strokes to mix (the mixing work). Fewer
   than 3 strokes do not mix a well. A stroke of the whole well draws air at the bottom and
   foams the liquid. Integra draws over 80% of the well five times; three mixes gave 11.8%
   CV where twenty gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at the concentration you
   calculated, and in a dilution series every later step inherits the error.
   Affected: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 4.
   Fix: Mix the well with about 80% of its volume (40 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5, 40,
   well)`. A stroke of the whole well draws air; use no more than 90%.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Integra: three serial-dilution protocols (over 80% of the volume, five times)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/3-simple-and-proven-automation-protocols-serial-dilutions-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   Source: Beckman AMPure XP instructions (mix with a tip volume just below the well volume)
           https://research.fredhutch.org/content/dam/research/hahn/methods/Agencourt%20AMPure%20XP.pdf
   Source: Esca Automation: serial dilution, a classic technique
           https://escaautomation.substack.com/p/serial-dilution-a-classic-technique
   Source: labautomation.io 3654: how to mix a bacteria sample enough
           https://labautomation.io/t/how-to-mix-bacteria-sample-enough/3654
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   [32f98f7767bb]

3. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No blank on a dilution series: 7 wells of bsa
   line 46:  p300.dispense(bsa_vol, dest)
   At line 46 the robot starts a dilution series of bsa in NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat
   (slot 4): 7 wells at 7 concentrations, each level about 2 times weaker than the one
   before. No well on this plate holds water with no sample, so there is no blank: the curve
   has no zero to read against, and a signal from the diluent or the plastic cannot be told
